sources: Design Reports/Rev3.0/Rev3.0_BOM_Ozdisan_100pcs.csv (part numbers, stock, MOQ, prices, links; generated 2026-11-13 by tools/make_bom_ozdisan.py from tools/bom_ozdisan_input.json)
Design Reports/Rev3.0/Rev3.0_BOM.csv (schematic references, values and links; exported 2026-11-12, before the 2026-11-13 schematic substitutions)
Design Reports/Rev3.0/Rev3.0_Design_Specification.md (function of each circuit block; display panel price §2)
Design Reports/Rev3.0/Rev3.0_GlassFront_Design.md (display panel and FPC tails J10/J11; glass-front cost estimate §0.3)
Design Reports/Rev3.0/tools/glassfront/overview/electronics_bom_input.json (hand-written group titles, roles, part texts, notes)
price_basis: Özdisan's US-dollar prices read on ozdisan.com on 2026-11-12, each part at the price break of its order quantity for 100 boards, with the HS1 heatsink at DigiKey's 2.60 USD and the TC1 probe at Motorobit's 145.86 TL (50.3 TL/USD) as recorded in the same sourced BOM; all figures are USD per board.

notes: Component total = sum of line_usd_per_board over all groups = 32.0880 USD, i.e. 32.09 USD per board, the same as the total stated in Rev3.0_BOM_Ozdisan_100pcs.md (32.09). Including the minimum-order rounding (what 100 boards actually cost, divided by 100) the sourced CSV gives 32.0927 USD, also 32.09.

Included: every purchased part of the board, the 4 fuse clips (not drawn in the schematic), the HS1 heatsink (DigiKey) and the TC1 thermocouple probe (Motorobit). Parts not bought from Özdisan: 5.50 USD of the total.

Not included: the display panel, the bare PCB, assembly and test, the glass-front module, the 1 kW heater element and the fan (oven parts), VAT, shipping and customs. The panel, PCB, assembly and glass front are listed under not_in_component_total.
lines = 80: 76 priced lines from the sourced CSV plus 4 schematic references with nothing to buy (J3, J4, R1, V1; status NOT_SOURCED, no price).
placements = 146 pieces mounted on each board (142 schematic parts plus 4 fuse clips). The sum of qty over all lines is 151: it also counts the off-board probe TC1 and the four unpriced references.

Status SUBSTITUTE means the bought part differs from the value or part number in Rev3.0_BOM.csv, upgrades such as a higher voltage rating included; the note says how. The KiCad schematic already carries these substitutions (Design Specification §12.7, 2026-11-13), but Rev3.0_BOM.csv was exported on 2026-11-12 and not re-exported.

VAT: the sourced BOM does not say whether the Özdisan prices of 2026-11-12 include VAT (the Design Specification §2 gives its earlier Özdisan prices excluding VAT); the probe price excludes VAT (KDV).

groups.title: Mains input, fuses and noise filter
groups.what_it_does: The 230 V mains enters the board here. Fuses and a surge absorber protect the oven, and a filter stops electrical noise from the heater switching from travelling back into the wall socket.

lines.role: Main fuse: cuts the mains if the oven draws too much current

lines.part: 100 µH 5 A power choke (filter coil), radial
lines.role: Main noise-filter coil; carries the full heater current

lines.part: 1 µF 275 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
lines.role: Works with the filter coil to soak up mains noise

lines.part: 100 nF 275 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
lines.role: Soaks up higher-frequency noise between the two mains wires

lines.part: Varistor (surge absorber), 275 VAC class, 14 mm disc
lines.role: Clamps voltage spikes from the mains, such as lightning surges
Protects the branch that feeds the 5 V power module
lines.note: Reomax STC1A250V instead of TBC1100A (out of stock); same 1 A time-lag rating.

lines.role: Keeps noise from the 5 V power module out of the mains

groups.title: Low-voltage power supply
groups.what_it_does: A sealed mains-to-5 V module powers the whole board. Two small converters then turn the 5 V into 3.3 V for the chips and 1.2 V for the core of the display controller.

lines.part: AC/DC power module, 90–245 VAC in, 5 V 2 A (10 W) out
lines.role: Turns mains into safe, isolated 5 V for the whole board
lines.note: Rated for 60 °C ambient; this module sets the board's 60 °C rating (every other part is chosen for 85 °C).

lines.role: Energy reservoir on the 5 V output of the power module
lines.note: Same 220 µF 16 V in a shorter can (6.3 × 7 mm instead of the 6.3 × 11 mm Koshin PKLH in the schematic link); fits the same footprint.

lines.part: Step-down converter chip, 5 V → 3.3 V, 2 A
lines.role: Makes the 3.3 V supply for processor, display and sensor chips
Energy-storage coil of the 3.3 V converter
Smooth the 5 V input of the 3.3 V and backlight converters
lines.note: C330/C331 at the 3.3 V converter input, C124/C127 in the backlight converter's input filter. Same part number as C116, C122, C336.

lines.role: Smooth the 3.3 V output of the converter
lines.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 10 V (the 10 V part is not in stock).

lines.role: Sets the converter's output to 3.3 V (together with R331)
Sets the converter's output to 3.3 V (together with R330)
Makes 1.2 V for the core of the display controller

groups.title: Heater switching and mains timing
groups.what_it_does: The processor turns the 1 kW heater on and off through an electronic power switch (a triac). Optical couplers keep the mains side electrically separated from the low-voltage side, and a detector tells the processor when the mains voltage crosses zero, so the heater is switched at the gentlest moment.

lines.part: Triac 25 A 800 V, insulated TO-220 (electronic power switch)
lines.role: Switches the 1 kW heater on and off
Lets the processor fire the triac while staying isolated from mains
lines.note: MOC3052 instead of MOC3053M (not stocked); it needs more LED current, hence R4 = 120 Ω. The KiCad value reads MOC3052M; the part bought is Isocom MOC3052X.

lines.role: Sets the current through the opto-triac's built-in LED
lines.note: 120 Ω instead of 200 Ω because U5 changed to the MOC3052. Already in the KiCad schematic since 2026-11-13; Rev3.0_BOM.csv was exported before that.

lines.role: Limit the triac's trigger current on the mains side

lines.part: 10 nF 305 VAC X2 safety film capacitor
lines.role: With R5, softens voltage spikes across the triac
With C4, softens voltage spikes across the triac

lines.part: Varistor (surge absorber), 350 VAC class, 10 mm disc
lines.role: Clamps surges across the triac to protect it
Detects each mains zero crossing, isolated from the mains
Feed a tiny mains current into the zero-cross detector

lines.part: Single logic inverter with Schmitt-trigger input, SOT-23-5
lines.role: Turns the zero-cross pulse into a clean digital signal
lines.note: Bought SN74AHC1G14DBVR; schematic value is SN74LVC1G14DBVR. Same single Schmitt-trigger inverter and pinout. The sourced BOM does not mark this as a substitution.

lines.role: Series resistor on the zero-cross signal to the processor

groups.title: Fan switching
groups.what_it_does: A small relay switches the oven's mains-powered fan. The processor drives the relay through a transistor.

lines.part: Relay, 5 V coil, changeover contact, 7 A
lines.role: Switches the oven fan on mains voltage
lines.note: Tianbo HJR-3FF instead of Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C (not stocked); same footprint and pinout, 7 A contacts (the relay only switches the fan).

lines.role: Lets the processor switch the relay coil current
Absorbs the relay coil's voltage spike at switch-off
lines.note: 1N4148W (Panjit) instead of MMSD4148T1G (out of stock); same kind of diode.

lines.role: Limits the processor's drive current into the transistor

groups.title: Processor and programming port
groups.what_it_does: The ESP32 module is the brain of the controller: it runs the temperature control, the touch screen and Wi-Fi. A 6-pin header lets a USB adapter load new software.

lines.part: ESP32-WROOM-32E module, Wi-Fi + Bluetooth, 16 MB flash
lines.role: Main processor: runs control, display, touch and Wi-Fi
Smooth the 3.3 V supply right at the processor
lines.note: The schematic link was Viking MCF02KTB250104 (100 nF 25 V), out of stock; one Yageo 100 nF 50 V part is bought for every 100 nF 0402 place on the board.

lines.role: With a resistor, holds the processor in reset until power is stable
lines.note: Value changed 100 nF → 1 µF (owner decision 2026-11-13, Espressif's recommendation for the reset delay). The KiCad schematic shows 1 µF; Rev3.0_BOM.csv was exported before the change.

lines.role: Local energy reservoir for the processor's Wi-Fi current bursts
Programming port for a USB-to-serial (FTDI) adapter
Let the programming adapter reset and restart the processor
lines.note: MMBT4401 instead of S8050 (not stocked); same pinout, 600 mA 40 V.

lines.role: Hold control lines at a defined level when nothing drives them
lines.note: Used in several circuits: R8/R10 zero-cross signal, R11–R14 programming reset, R15 fan transistor, R124 display chip, R224 temperature chip.

lines.role: Keep the data bus to touch and sensor chips at its idle level
lines.note: Pull-up resistors of the two-wire I²C bus shared by the touch controller and the temperature converter.

groups.title: Display controller
groups.what_it_does: The processor cannot drive a 7-inch screen on its own. A dedicated display chip keeps the whole picture in its own memory and sends it to the screen about 60 times a second; small resistors on the fast data lines keep the signals clean and reduce radio interference.

lines.part: Display controller SSD1963 with picture memory, LQFP-128
lines.role: Stores the picture and drives the 7-inch screen
Clock reference for the display controller
Let the crystal run at exactly 10 MHz
Soften the fast data signals from processor to display chip
Soften the 28 picture signals to the screen, cutting radio interference
Smooth the supply right at the display chip, screen, touch and sensor
lines.note: Upgrade: 50 V instead of 16 V, same 100 nF. C112–C115 and C117–C119 at the display chip, C123 screen supply, C126 touch supply, C223/C225/C226 temperature circuit.

lines.role: Larger smoothing capacitors on the display and 1.2 V supplies
lines.note: Upgrade: 10 V instead of 6.3 V. C116 at the display chip, C122 screen supply, C336 at the 1.2 V regulator output.

lines.role: Smooth the 1.2 V core supply of the display chip
lines.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 6.3 V. C120/C121 at the display chip's 1.2 V pins, C337 at the 1.2 V regulator output.

groups.title: Screen connection, backlight and touch
groups.what_it_does: Two flat-cable connectors link the board to the screen and to its touch layer. A small boost converter makes the roughly 9.6 V that lights the screen's LED backlight, with the brightness set by the display chip, and tiny protection diodes guard the touch lines (and the probe input) against static electricity.

lines.part: 40-pin flat-cable (FPC) connector, 0.5 mm pitch, top contact
lines.role: Takes the screen's flat cable: picture signals and backlight power

lines.part: 6-pin flat-cable (FPC) connector, 0.5 mm pitch, top contact
lines.role: Takes the touch panel's flat cable
Raises 5 V to about 9.6 V for the screen's LED backlight
Energy-storage coil of the backlight converter

lines.part: Schottky diode SS14, 1 A 40 V, SMA
lines.role: One-way valve for current in the backlight converter
lines.note: Same SS14 type made by Jiaqi; the ON Semiconductor / Panjit versions are not stocked.

lines.role: Smooths the backlight converter's output
lines.note: 50 V X5R instead of 25 V X7R (no 25 V X7R 0805 in stock); the 50 V part keeps more of its capacitance at the 9.6 V it sees.

lines.role: Limits the voltage if the backlight is disconnected
Measure the backlight current so it stays at 138 mA
lines.note: Precision 0.1 % thin-film part, the only 18 Ω 0805 in stock; better than needed.

lines.role: Wire links in the backlight control path
Keeps the backlight off until the display chip is ready
Filter coil that keeps backlight noise off the 5 V supply
lines.note: 10 µH instead of 2.2 µH (the 2.2 µH part is not stocked); same part as L11, the filter still works (corner 34 → 16 kHz).

lines.role: Stops the backlight's input filter from oscillating (with C128)
lines.note: Upgrade: 1 % 0.5 W instead of 0.25 W. The sourced BOM names a cheaper 5 % 0.25 W alternative (Uniohm RR1206J050KT5E, 0.046 USD).

lines.part: 47 µF 16 V electrolytic capacitor, SMD 5 × 5.8 mm
lines.role: Stops the backlight's input filter from oscillating (with R132)
lines.note: Upgrade: 16 V instead of 10 V, can 5.8 mm tall instead of 5.4 mm, same footprint. Özdisan stock 316, enough for 100 boards.

lines.role: Noise filter on the backlight wires; helper for the 3.3 V converter
lines.note: Upgrade: 50 V instead of 25 V. C129 sits at the screen connector, C332 belongs to the 3.3 V converter.

lines.role: Give radio-frequency noise a short path to ground at the connectors
Feed 3.3 V to the screen and to the touch panel
Protect touch and probe lines against static electricity
lines.note: D112/D113/D115/D116 at the touch connector, D220/D221 at the thermocouple terminal. The link is Özdisan's site search for the part number, which opens the product page when the search has a single hit; the repo has no direct product-page link.

groups.title: Temperature measurement
groups.what_it_does: A thermocouple probe in the oven produces a tiny voltage that grows with temperature. A precise 16-bit converter chip measures it, a small thermistor measures the terminal's own temperature to correct the reading, and filters remove noise picked up along the probe cable.

lines.role: Measures the probe's tiny voltage very precisely
Connection point for the thermocouple probe wires
Measures the terminal's own temperature to correct the reading
lines.note: Thinking TSM1B103F3381RZ instead of Murata NCP18XH103F03RB (not stocked); same 10 kΩ 1 % B 3380 K in 0603.

lines.role: Part of the noise filter on the probe input
Filters noise between the two probe wires
Filter noise picked up equally on both probe wires
lines.note: Less precise type: X7R 10 % instead of C0G 1 % (no 10 nF C0G 0603 in stock). The Design Specification §6 works the noise case with a 10 % mismatch; the sourced BOM calls it acceptable.

lines.role: Make a disconnected or broken probe show up as an error
Reference resistors for the thermistor measurement
Smooth the supply of the converter chip and the 1.2 V regulator
lines.note: C224 at the temperature converter chip, C335 at the 1.2 V regulator input. Same part number as C120, C121, C337.

groups.title: Cooling and mechanical parts
groups.what_it_does: Metal hardware without electronics: the tall heatsink that carries the heat away from the heater switch, and the clips that hold the two replaceable glass fuses.

lines.part: Aluminium heatsink 45 × 12.7 × 63.5 mm with solder pins, for TO-220
lines.role: Carries away the heater switch's heat, about 3.7 W
lines.note: Not sold by Özdisan (its largest TO-220 heatsink is 35 mm); bought from DigiKey, minimum order 5.

lines.part: Fuse clip for 5 × 20 mm fuses, PCB mount
lines.role: Hold the two glass fuses so they can be replaced
lines.note: Not drawn in the schematic: 2 clips per fuse, 4 per board. The clip pin diameter against the 1.3 mm footprint holes is still to be confirmed.

groups.title: Probe, heater and wire connections
groups.what_it_does: Items that are not soldered parts of the board: the temperature probe that goes into the oven, the heater element itself, and the bare pads where the mains and fan cables are soldered on.

lines.part: K-type thermocouple probe, M6 ring tip, 1 m lead, 0–600 °C
lines.role: Senses the oven temperature; its wires screw into J20
lines.note: Motorobit shows stock '10+' against 100 needed: ask Motorobit for 100 pieces. Price 145.86 TL + VAT at 50.3 TL/USD (2026-11-12). Özdisan sells no thermocouple probes.

lines.part: 1 kW heater element (part of the oven)
lines.role: Heats the oven; switched on and off by the triac Q1
lines.note: Oven-side part, not part of the electronics; there is no supplier line for it in the repo. It is soldered to the board's heater pads.

lines.part: Solder pads for the mains cable (no part)
lines.role: Where the mains cable (live and neutral) is soldered on
lines.note: Nothing to buy: bare pads on the board.

lines.part: Solder pads for the fan cable (no part)
lines.role: Where the oven fan's cable is soldered on
lines.note: Nothing to buy: bare pads on the board. The fan itself is an oven part.

lines.role: Stands for the wall socket in circuit simulations only
lines.note: Nothing to buy. The schematic's link for V1 points to the ngspice simulator manual, not to a product, so no link is given.
